name: insw
synopsis: void insw(unsigned short port, void *addr, unsigned long count);
description: insw performs a series of word-sized input operations from the specified I/O port to memory. It is used for low-level hardware access and requires proper permissions via ioperm or iopl.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The I/O port to read from

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Pointer to the memory buffer where data will be stored

return_value.failure: Causes segmentation fault if the process does not have permission to access the I/O ports

errors.description: Segmentation fault occurs if ioperm(2) or iopl(2) has not been used to grant access

bugs: These functions require compilation with optimization flags like -O or -O2, as they are defined as inline macros. Additionally, the argument order is hardware-specific and opposite to most DOS implementations.
